description: In both the editor's live preview and the full Preview page, the user sees exactly where each printed A4 page ends and the next one begins. The marking stays discreet and follows every change to the CV content or layout without a reload.

userStories.title: Page boundaries visible in the editor's live preview
userStories.description: As a user editing a CV, I want to see where each printed page ends in the live preview, so that I can adjust my content while I write.
acceptanceCriteria: When the unscaled document height is more than one `PAGE_HEIGHT_PX`, the live preview shows one indicator at each unscaled y = k × `PAGE_HEIGHT_PX` (k = 1 … pages − 1). Each indicator lies within 1 px of that position, after applying `previewScale`.
A document that fits on one page shows no indicator. This includes `professional` and `modern` at their minimum height of exactly one page.
Each indicator carries a localized label naming the page that starts below it (« Page 2 », « Page 3 », …), in the editor's current locale (`fr`, `en`, `de`, `it`).

Adding content that pushes the document past a page edge makes a new indicator appear without a reload. Removing that content makes it disappear. Also covered: changing a layout setting that changes the document height, such as font scale.
The indicator never covers or intercepts the CV. Clicks and text selection inside the preview behave as without it (`pointer-events: none`). The label is not drawn over CV text.
The indicator stays aligned at every preview scale the editor supports, including the narrow-screen layout and after the split divider is dragged.
The indicator is outside `data-testid="resume-document"` and hidden in print media.

FR-1: One shared computation, from the measured unscaled document height and `PAGE_HEIGHT_PX`, gives the page count and the boundary positions for both surfaces. It uses the existing constants in `src/lib/resume-page-size.ts`; no second page-height value is introduced.

FR-2: The count rule is pages = max(1, ceil(height / `PAGE_HEIGHT_PX`)), with a sub-pixel tolerance so that a document exactly one page tall (± 1 px) counts as one page. US-003 is the authority: if the printed PDF disagrees on a fixture, the rule is wrong.
FR-3: The indicator is derived state only. It is computed from the rendered DOM and is never persisted, never written into the resume or layout model, and never sent to an export.
FR-4: The indicator is discreet: a thin line plus a small label, visually lighter than the CV content. Its exact styling is validated by `ui-expert` on the rendered result.
FR-5: The page label uses the existing dictionary under `resumes.*`, with all four locales filled in. No string is hardcoded.

Regression constraint: `data-testid="resume-document"` renders pixel-identically to today on screen and in print for all five templates. Evidence: `pnpm test:visual` passes with its existing baselines; no baseline is updated.
Regression constraint: `pnpm test:parity` stays at MATCH 206 / KNOWN 3 / NEW 0 on Windows.
Regression constraint: `e2e/resume-print-geometry.spec.ts` and `e2e/modern-long-sidebar-print.spec.ts` pass unchanged.
Regression constraint: The editor preview frame keeps its current scaling, height tracking and responsive behavior. Evidence: `e2e/resume-editor-responsive.spec.ts` passes unchanged.
Regression constraint: The page count of a printed PDF does not change for any template.
Regression constraint: The DOCX generators and their output are not touched.
Verification: The CLAUDE.md §14 baseline, run on the final diff: typecheck, test, test:integration, test:e2e, build (or build:verify) and lint. Lint is judged against the ceiling of 306 problems.
Verification: `pnpm test:visual` and `pnpm test:parity`, for the regression constraints above.
Verification: New e2e coverage for US-001, US-002 and US-003, run in the `test:e2e` suite.
Verification: Unit tests for the computation in FR-1, including the boundary cases: exactly one page, one page + 1 px, one page − 1 px; exactly two pages; a height of 0 or not yet measured.

Verification: Rendered browser evidence (screenshots) reviewed by `ui-expert`: the editor at desktop width and at a narrow width, with a two-page CV; the Preview page with a three-page CV; one locale other than `en`.
Verification: A PDF printed from the Preview page, opened and checked: no indicator or label on any page, and the page count is unchanged.
FAIL condition: The number of indicators + 1 differs from the printed PDF page count for any template fixture.
FAIL condition: An indicator sits more than 1 px (unscaled) from k × `PAGE_HEIGHT_PX`.
FAIL condition: The indicator or its label appears in a printed PDF, a `test:visual` capture of `resume-document`, or a DOCX.
FAIL condition: Any `test:visual` baseline needs updating, or `test:parity` reports NEW > 0 or a changed MATCH / KNOWN count.
FAIL condition: The indicator blocks a click or text selection in the preview, or covers CV text.
FAIL condition: An indicator does not appear or disappear after a content or layout change until the page is reloaded.
FAIL condition: The label is missing or untranslated in any of `fr`, `en`, `de`, `it`.
BLOCKER condition: The local Supabase stack or the e2e authentication fixture is unavailable, so the editor and Preview cannot be exercised.
BLOCKER condition: The printed PDF page count cannot be obtained in the e2e environment, so US-003 cannot be proven.

BLOCKER condition: A template fixture's PDF page count cannot be reconciled with ceil(height / `PAGE_HEIGHT_PX`) without changing print CSS. That would contradict Out of Scope, so it returns to the owner.
Out of scope: Changing where the PDF breaks pages: no `break-inside`/`break-before` rules and no orphan or widow control.
Out of scope: Inserting real gaps or splitting the preview into separate sheets. The document stays one continuous sheet, so its layout, and therefore the parity measurements, do not move.
Out of scope: A page count or the indicator in the DOCX export. Word paginates on its own.
Out of scope: Any change to the DOCX generators, the parity harness verdicts, the layout model or the database.
Out of scope: Predicting the small downward shift caused by a line that straddles a sheet edge. The indicator marks the sheet edge itself (see Risks).
Out of scope: Redesigning the editor toolbar, the Preview header or the preview frame.

userStories.title: The indicator count matches the printed PDF for every template
userStories.description: As the product owner, I want automated proof that the indicator is precise, so that it cannot drift from the real PDF pagination.
acceptanceCriteria: An e2e test renders the Preview page for each of the five templates, with one one-page fixture and one fixture of at least two pages. It generates the print PDF of that page. It asserts that (number of indicators + 1) equals the number of PDF pages.
The same test asserts that the editor live preview of the same resume shows the same number of indicators as the Preview page.
The fixtures are deterministic test data and contain no real user data.
